acceptance: Rust domain tests cover assign, accept, submit-proof, parent approve/return, why answer, ledger append, repair, and invalid transitions.
Frontend contract exposes child mode and parent mode with no payment controls and a three-step child flow.
All state transitions are append-only events with deterministic ledger totals and repair paths.
Baseline and modified test commands, diff, verification, and rollback artifacts are retained.
Progress active.json marks implementation complete at 80/100 while verification and delivery remain pending.
metric: offline vertical-slice domain tests pass and implementation progress reaches 80/100 without external effects
non_goals: No provider or network integration, no real child data, no deployment or publication.
No payment, authentication provider, object storage, AI voice, or remote notification implementation.
No Git mutation and no dependency installation from the network.
outcome: Implement a bounded offline-first vertical slice for the WeChat mini-program MVP: task lifecycle transitions, proof submission metadata, parent review, one why-question, reward ledger entries, repairable consequences, and a minimal child/parent UI contract scaffold.
problem: The governance and product plans are materialized but the project has no executable implementation for the core child-parent task loop.
rollback: Restore all pre-existing declared paths from recorded hashes and remove only newly created source/test/docs paths; verify rollback on a disposable copy and preserve governance receipts.
rollout: Preview and apply the bounded implementation plan, create source and test files, run baseline and modified tests offline, rehearse rollback on a disposable copy, then run doctor and full checks.
